title: chore: remove legacy image backend root
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Removes the remaining image.pollinations.ai directory after active GPU workers moved into operations/infrastructure/gpu.
- Deletes retired SANA-Sprint and LTX-2 implementations, the unreferenced TwinFlow experiment, obsolete AWS/io.net Flux tooling, and old service assets.
- Removes the completed PR #7807 rotation checklist and obsolete image-service test command.
- Updates repository architecture, monitoring, debugging, deployment guidance, and social path classification.
- Does not change the public https://image.pollinations.ai hostname, model registry, routing, credentials, pricing, or live GPUs.

Safety evidence:
- Deleted backends have no current registry or workflow consumers.
- SANA-Sprint and LTX-2 are documented as retired.
- Current FLUX, Z-Image, Klein, and DreamShaper sources exist in the preceding stacked PRs.
- Non-URL references to the deleted root are zero.

Validation:
- DreamShaper unit tests
- operations deployment-detection tests
- shell syntax checks for all active GPU scripts
- repository path/reference scans
- git diff --check

Stacked on #13244. Merge the stack in order. Existing GPU hosts must not pull the moved checkout until their setup script is rerun from its new path.

gist.headline: Old roots, clean garden
gist.blurb: The retired image backend root has been composted after its GPU workers settled into their new home. The public image hostname and live model garden keep humming exactly as before.
gist.summary: Removed the legacy image.pollinations.ai source tree, including retired SANA-Sprint and LTX-2 backends, TwinFlow, obsolete Flux deployment tooling, and outdated operational docs now that active GPU workers live under operations/infrastructure/gpu.
gist.impact: Public image.pollinations.ai routing, model registry, credentials, pricing, and live GPUs remain unchanged, while maintainers get one current location for active GPU infrastructure.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy garden-shed cleanup: Polli gently carries a labeled box of retired server scripts toward a compost bin while healthy GPU code-plants grow from the new operations/infrastructure/gpu path on a glowing CRT terminal. The scene represents removing unreferenced historical infrastructure without disturbing the active image service; a small sign reassures that the public image gateway is still blooming.
